claims.claim: SolarEdge links distributed solar generation and storage to household/commercial electricity needs through inverter and power-electronics control; recovery in revenue and gross margin indicates improved conversion of that installed-market role into operating economics.

Data-center power is an adjacency rather than a proven causal extension: the transferable capability is power conversion/control, but customer requirements, architectures and competitive sets differ from residential/commercial solar.

factors.name: scenarioRobustness
factors.basis: Core solar/storage recovery provides the present base while data-center power is optionality, not required proof of current recovery.

factors.name: substitutionResilience
factors.basis: Module-level and inverter architectures compete with alternative string/central inverter and storage-control designs.

factors.name: bottleneckControl
factors.basis: Power electronics are necessary infrastructure, but SolarEdge does not uniquely control the solar or data-center power bottleneck.

causalEdges.to: demand for power conversion and control
causalEdges.mechanism: generation/storage assets require inverter and energy-management infrastructure
higher revenue and gross margin reduce the fragility created by the prior downturn
high-growth compute infrastructure also requires efficient power conversion/control

risks.risk: A successor bottleneck can shift from inverter availability to end-market financing, grid interconnection, storage economics or customer acquisition.

unknowns.unknown: Durability of recovery through a full demand/inventory cycle and commercial traction in data-center power remain unproven.

claims.claim: The turnaround is materially supported by revenue, margin and operating-loss improvement, but remains incomplete because GAAP losses persisted and the evidence does not establish full-cycle durability.

factors.name: turnaround durability
factors.basis: Six consecutive quarters of year-over-year margin expansion strengthen the recovery case, while GAAP profitability and full-cycle durability remain incomplete.

factors.name: adjacency confidence
factors.basis: Data-center power should not be capitalized as an established growth engine before customer and revenue evidence exists.

risks.risk: Solar demand cyclicality and inventory corrections can reverse operating leverage.
Competitive power-electronics alternatives can constrain pricing and share recovery.

unknowns.unknown: Current evidence does not quantify data-center pipeline, customer wins or margins.
